newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power eases ahead of milder weekend.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power eases ahead of milder weekend.

text.p: Wholesale electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. were mostly softer Friday ahead of the weekend and forecasts for milder weather through Monday, industry sources said.
"It's very quiet. The weather is slowly warming up in the South," said one power marketer, adding that a forecasted return of cooler weather late next week could boost prices.
At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak power prices for Saturday and Sunday were talked lower in the $19.00-21.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) area, as compared to Thursday's discussion around $26.00.
For Monday delivery, however, peak prices held mostly steady in the $25.75-26.00 area.
Some traders noted that stronger spot natural gas prices in the Gulf to the mid-$2.70s to $2.80 per million British thermal units were helping to sustain current electricity price levels.
Firm, off-peak at the Ga./Fla. border for next-day delivery remained flat in the $16.00-$18.00 range.
Among Florida utilities, peak, firm electricity scheduled for the weekend was valued again in the $24.00-25.00 area, but trading was light.
Peak, firm power for Saturday and Sunday delivery into northwestern portion of Tennessee Valley Authority's (TVA) territory were pegged around $18.00, down from Thursday's $23.00 level.
For Monday delivery, peak, firm power traded around $19.50.
Firm, off-peak power prices remained steady in the $14.75-15.00 area, traders said.
